page: OVHcloud rtx5000-56 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine within the Cloud GPU family, hosted on the KVM hypervisor. The compute configuration delivers 8 dedicated x86_64 physical cores using the Intel Xeon W-3235 processor operating at a base frequency of 3.3 GHz without hyperthreading. Memory capacity totals 56 GB of system RAM, allocating 7 GB per dedicated core. Graphic and machine learning acceleration is provided by two discrete NVIDIA Turing RTX 5000 GPUs with 32 GB of combined GDDR6 VRAM (16 GB per card). High-speed local persistence consists of 400 GB SSD storage, paired with a 4 Gbps baseline network uplink.

Benchmark results demonstrate specialized acceleration for artificial intelligence workloads. In small (135M) and medium (7B) parameter large language model inference tests, the dual Turing GPUs achieve top-tier throughput, processing prompts at up to 9506.12 tokens per second and generating 67.32 tokens per second on 7B models. System memory performance registers in the top 25% with a PassMark memory score of 2838.84. In contrast, general host compute metrics fall largely within the median tier, showing a Geekbench multi-core score of 6948 and PassMark CPU score of 14005.52, while uncached write bandwidth and single-threaded gzip compression exhibit lower-quartile performance.

The hardware balance makes the rtx5000-56 cost efficient for dual-GPU acceleration workloads requiring moderate host memory without the capital overhead of enterprise data center accelerators. However, the 8-core CPU allocation and 32 GB total VRAM partition constrain utility for training or running 70B parameter models, where prompt evaluation drops to 16.92 tokens per second. The instance is best suited for medium LLM inference, 3D rendering, computer vision pipelines, parallelized model testing, and GPU-accelerated video transcode workflows.
description: OVHcloud rtx5000-56 is a specialized cloud virtual machine engineered for GPU-accelerated computing. Powered by an 8-core Intel Xeon W-3235 processor at 3.3 GHz with dedicated x86_64 execution threads, the instance incorporates 56 GB of system RAM and 400 GB of local SSD storage alongside a 4 Gbps network baseline. Acceleration is driven by dual NVIDIA Turing RTX 5000 GPUs providing 32 GB of total VRAM. In benchmark testing, the platform achieves top-tier throughput for small and medium-scale LLM inference, delivering up to 9506 tokens per second for prompt processing, while general CPU execution and memory subsystem metrics remain consistent with median multi-core expectations. The machine exhibits trade-offs in uncached write throughput and large 70B parameter generation capabilities. The rtx5000-56 is suited for distributed inference of models up to 7B parameters, computer vision workloads, real-time 3D rendering, and GPU-driven batch processing.
